title: Counting 1 to 20

parent.learn: Say one number for each thing, touching it as you go.
parent.why: Little children often say numbers faster than they point. Touching each thing once joins one number-word to one object, so nothing is skipped or counted twice.

parent.learn: The last number you say tells how many there are.
parent.why: Counting answers the question “how many?”. The last number is the size of the whole group, not the name of the last thing.

parent.learn: Read and write the numerals 0 to 20.
parent.why: A numeral is a short way to write an amount. Matching 5 to five things joins the word, the symbol and the amount.

parent.learn: See small amounts at a glance, like the dots on a dice.
parent.why: Seeing 3 or 5 without counting (it is called subitising) makes adding quicker later: if you see 5 at once, 5 + 2 is just “6, 7”.
An empty plate still has a number of sweets on it: 0. Zero is where counting starts on the number line.

rounds.t: The basket is empty. How many mangoes are in it?
rounds.h: Empty means nothing is there, and nothing is zero: 0.

rounds.t: How many fingers are on one hand?
rounds.h: Count them: thumb 1, then 2, 3, 4, 5. One hand has 5 fingers.
